title_en: Xibao Group Holding Co., Ltd. v. Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch — dispute over bank settlement contract
ruling_gist_en: Where the names of the designated payee and the actual payee are not completely consistent on the surface, but such inconsistency does not cause ambiguity according to legal provisions, it shall not be deemed as a discrepancy. Cross-border settlement acts only constitute a condition of the underlying transaction; the direct cause of the loss lies in the conduct of the debtor in the underlying transaction. In the absence of an objective and necessary causal link between the settlement act and the loss, the settlement bank shall not bear compensation liability.

full_text_en:
Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited v. Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch — dispute over bank settlement contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where the designated payee and the actual payee are not entirely identical in name on the surface, but according to legal provisions, this does not give rise to ambiguity, it shall not be deemed as a discrepancy. Cross-border settlement acts merely constitute a condition for the underlying transaction; the direct cause of the loss lies in the conduct of the debtor in the underlying transaction. There is no objective and inevitable causal connection between the settlement act and the loss, and the settlement bank shall not bear liability for compensation.

Plaintiff: Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited (Chinese name: 喜宝集团控股有限公司), domiciled at: Luen Cheong Street, Fanling Union Market, New Territories, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Liu Jiaxin, Director of the company.

Defendant: Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, domiciled at: Zhengyang Road, Chengyang District, Qingdao City, Shandong Province.
Person in Charge: Yin Huijian, Branch Manager.

The plaintiff, Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited (Chinese name: 喜宝集团控股有限公司, hereinafter referred to as Lucky Pearl Group), filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province against the defendant, Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch), over a dispute over a bank settlement contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On March 30, 2009, it remitted a total of USD 5,000,000 in three installments through Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited to the defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, as agreed. The remittance application forms indicated the payee as "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Co., Ltd." The defendant, knowing that this name did not match the name "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company," neither made necessary inquiries before settlement nor proactively returned the remittance, but settled the payment on March 31, 2009. In particular, when the plaintiff applied for return of the remittance through the remitting bank, Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited, on April 6, 2009, and April 15, 2009, and personally requested the defendant to stop payment, the defendant still converted the funds into RMB, causing the plaintiff's USD 5,000,000 to be exchanged into RMB and enter circulation. Of this amount, USD 3,710,000 was illegally possessed by Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company and quickly transferred, and the company's personnel became untraceable. Having no other choice, the plaintiff sued that company in the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province. The court ruled against that company, but by then, the company's legal representative, Chen Jianrong, was wanted online by a public security authority in another location on suspicion of fraud. The court only recovered USD 1,290,000 in enforcement. As the company had no other executable assets, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province rendered an Enforcement Termination Ruling on September 10, 2010 [ (2010) Qing Zhi Zi No. 195 ], terminating the enforcement of that case. Since the defendant's serious violation of foreign exchange business operating procedures had a causal relationship with the plaintiff's huge foreign exchange loss, the defendant should bear compensation liability to the plaintiff. The plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to compensate the plaintiff for USD 3,710,000.

Defendant's Defense: First, the defendant's settlement procedures and results for the remittance were completely correct and error-free. On March 30, 2009, the defendant received three MT103 wire transfer messages from the remitting bank, showing remittance amounts of USD 1,800,000, USD 1,800,000, and USD 1,400,000, respectively, with the payee's account number 3810XXXXXXXXX4274, the payee's name as "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Co., Ltd.," and the remarks as "investment funds." The defendant, in accordance with business procedures, verified the payee's account information and found that the account was a foreign exchange capital account opened by Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company at the defendant's sub-branch with the approval of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. The payee's account number matched exactly the account number in the messages, the account holder was the payee indicated in the messages, and the nature of the account was a foreign exchange capital account. Since the account number, account holder, and account purpose all matched the remittance messages, the remittance could be uniquely and correctly identified, and the defendant settled the remittance into that account. The defendant's settlement procedures were free of any error, and the funds did not enter any wrong account. Second, the defendant had no obligation to proactively return the remittance. The account number and payee name in the remittance messages were clear and not ambiguous; the defendant could and should have settled the remittance on time based on the information in the messages. Naturally, the defendant had no obligation to proactively return the remittance. Third, the defendant's settlement operation realized the plaintiff's original intention for the remittance. On March 27, 2009, the plaintiff, Lucky Pearl Group, and Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company signed a foreign currency loan agreement. The plaintiff's remittance of USD 5,000,000 to Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company was the plaintiff's true intention, and the remittance act was the plaintiff's performance of the foreign currency loan agreement. The defendant's settlement operation not only completed the instruction in the remittance messages but also realized the plaintiff's original intention for the remittance. Fourth, the plaintiff's alleged loss was entirely caused by its own reasons and has no causal relationship with the defendant. Fifth, the plaintiff's unreasonable lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations. In the process of settling the remittance involved in this case, the defendant fulfilled its obligation of prudent and necessary examination, and there was no fault whatsoever. The plaintiff's alleged loss has no legal causal relationship with the defendant's settlement act, and the defendant should not bear any legal liability.

The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province found the following facts at first instance:

On March 30, 2009, the plaintiff, Lucky Pearl Group, applied to Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited to remit USD 1,800,000, USD 1,400,000, and USD 1,800,000 in three installments by wire from its foreign currency current savings deposit account numbered 0128XXXXXX8151 held at that bank. The remittance application forms recorded the remittance numbers as 1209033083004671, 1209033083004788, and 1209033083005094, respectively, the receiving bank as "Agricultural Bank of China Qingdao City Branch Chengyang District Sub-branch," the payee name as "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Co., Ltd.," the payee account number as 3810XXXXXXXXX4274, and the remarks to the payee as "investment funds." Accordingly, the remitting bank, Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited, sent MT103 wire transfer messages to the defendant, the receiving bank, on March 30, 2009, and the defendant received them on the same day.

Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company was a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (by a Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan legal person) established on March 11, 2009, initiated by Ruisheng Investment Co., Ltd., and on April 3, 2009, it obtained approval to add relevant import and export business to its business scope. On March 30, 2009, the International Business Department of the defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, printed credit advices in the system, stamped them with the "Business Completed" seal of the International Business Department of Agricultural Bank of China Qingdao Chengyang District Sub-branch, and credited the above three remittances to the foreign exchange capital account numbered 3810XXXXXXXXX4274 opened by Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company at the defendant's sub-branch. The credit advices recorded the declaration form numbers. The capital verification unit sent confirmation letters to the defendant and Qingdao Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, respectively. The defendant and Qingdao Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange confirmed the paid-in capital of Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company on March 30, 2009, and March 31, 2009, respectively. In its confirmation reply, Qingdao Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange specifically noted that "the payer and the investor are inconsistent." The capital verification unit issued a capital verification report on March 31, 2009, verifying and confirming the above USD 5,000,000 as the capital contribution of the shareholder of Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company.

On April 1, 2009, the plaintiff's legal representative, Liu Jiaxin, went to the defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, to check the accounts and discovered that Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company had forged the plaintiff's specimen seal, raising suspicion of fraud, and immediately made every effort to recover the funds. During the process of recovering the funds, the plaintiff's legal representative, Liu Jiaxin, was defrauded of money, and the relevant persons have been subject to criminal liability. The criminal judgment confirmed the facts described above. On April 6, 2009, the plaintiff applied to the remitting bank, Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited, for return of the USD 5,000,000 remitted on March 30, 2009, on the ground that the receiving company lacked the business scope. After receiving the message from the remitting bank, the defendant contacted Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company regarding the return of the remittance. On April 8, 2009, Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company objected to the return, stating that its capital source was lawful and its business was operating normally. On April 9, 2009, the defendant replied to the remitting bank, informing it that Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company did not agree to return the funds. On April 15, 2009, the plaintiff again applied to the remitting bank for return of the remittance, citing the payee name error as the reason, and the plaintiff's legal representative, Liu Jiaxin, together with another person, went to the defendant to arrange the return. On April 16, 2009, Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company submitted a written application to the defendant, stating that it had provided the defendant with a payee undertaking letter, undertaking that the three incoming remittances with the payee name "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Co., Ltd." were its foreign investment funds, the capital source was lawful, and the company's business was operating normally, and it did not agree to the return of the three foreign refund messages. On April 17, 2009, the defendant replied to the remitting bank, informing it that Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company refused the return of the remittance. Regarding the application for remittance and return of the USD 5,000,000 involved in this case, Henan Dazheng Law Firm sent an inquiry letter to the remitting bank in August 2011. Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited replied to the law firm on September 8, 2011, providing a detailed explanation of the process of handling the relevant business in accordance with the client's instructions.

The plaintiff, Lucky Pearl Group, and the defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, confirmed that the settlement date was March 30, 2009, and the defendant specified the conversion (conversion of foreign exchange into RMB) date as April 16, 2009.

It was further found that: In the case of the enterprise loan dispute between the plaintiff, Lucky Pearl Group, and Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province rendered a civil judgment on March 3, 2010 [ (2009) Qing Min Si Chu Zi No. 96 ], which has become legally effective. The plaintiff admitted that the USD 5,000,000 remitted in this case and the USD 5,000,000 adjudicated in that case were the same sum. The facts confirmed in the effective civil judgment of that case were: On March 27, 2009, the two parties signed a foreign currency loan agreement stipulating that, in connection with the enterprise's need to bring in foreign capital (foreign currency) from abroad to the domestic enterprise for short-term borrowing to handle relevant formalities, Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company and Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited reached the following loan agreement through negotiation: 1. Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company borrowed USD 10,000,000 from Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited and voluntarily paid a one-time fee of 6% of the total loan amount to Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited (including capital movement fees, exchange rate risk fees, handling fees, etc.); 2. The loan period was from March 30, 2009, to April 5, 2009; 3. To ensure the safety of Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited's funds, during the loan period, Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company must hand over all original documents and all company seals to Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited for control; 4. After completing the relevant formalities for the use of the foreign currency, Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company must fully cooperate with Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited to return the full amount of RMB equivalent after conversion of the foreign exchange to the account designated by Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited; 5. After Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited receives the full repayment into its account, it shall promptly and unconditionally return the original documents and company seals of Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company to it; 6. The above terms of this loan were voluntarily negotiated and agreed upon by both parties. Both parties shall comply, and if one party breaches, the breaching party shall compensate the other party for double the economic losses. After signing the contract, on March 30, 2009, Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited remitted USD 1,800,000, USD 1,800,000, and USD 1,400,000, totaling USD 5,000,000, in three installments from its account at Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited to Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company, with the receiving bank being Agricultural Bank of China Qingdao City Branch Chengyang District Sub-branch, and the "remarks to payee" column all indicated "investment funds." On the same day, after receiving the three sums, Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company engaged Qingdao Kangbang United Certified Public Accountants to send a confirmation letter to Qingdao Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange regarding the three sums. Qingdao Branch of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange issued a confirmation reply on March 31, 2009, stating that the foreign exchange capital account in question was opened with the approval of the bureau, the foreign investment foreign exchange registration date was March 31, 2009, and the payer and the investor were inconsistent. On April 3, 2009, Qingdao Municipal People's Government issued the Approval Certificate for Foreign Investment Enterprise of the People's Republic of China, Document No. Shang Wai Zi Qing Fu Zi [2009] 0302, recording a total investment of USD 10,000,000 and a registered capital of USD 10,000,000, with the investor name as Hong Kong Ruisheng Investment Co., Ltd. (Luck Sincere Investment Limited). In its trial of that case, this court held that the total investment and registered capital of Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company were both USD 10,000,000, which did not meet the conditions for borrowing foreign debt under the national "investment-difference" management principle, and it lacked the qualification to borrow foreign debt. Therefore, its act of borrowing foreign currency from Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited violated the relevant provisions of the state on foreign exchange control, and the foreign currency loan agreement should be deemed invalid. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, in its judgment in that case, ordered Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company to return the principal loan of USD 5,000,000 and pay interest of RMB 65,000 to Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited. As Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company failed to fulfill the obligations determined in the judgment, Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited applied for enforcement to the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province on May 31, 2010, with the enforcement target amount being RMB 34,289,125. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province deducted RMB 8,962,320.73 from the bank account of Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company, deducted and paid enforcement fees of RMB 101,689, and distributed the remaining amount to Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited. Subsequently, after extensive searching, no other executable assets of Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company could be found by the time the enforcement proceedings were terminated. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, on September 10, 2010, rendered an Enforcement Ruling [ (2010) Qing Zhi Zi No. 195 ], terminating the current enforcement proceedings under Civil Judgment (2009) Qing Min Si Chu Zi No. 96, and stating that the enforcement applicant, Lucky Pearl Group Holdings Limited, may apply to the people's court with jurisdiction for enforcement of the remaining creditor's rights when the conditions for enforcement are met.

It was further found that: The headquarters of Agricultural Bank of China issued the "Operating Procedures for Foreign Exchange Remittance Business of Agricultural Bank of China" on January 25, 2005. Article 2 of the said Operating Procedures stipulates: "For the purposes of these Operating Procedures, 'foreign exchange remittance' refers to the settlement method by which the bank pays a certain amount of foreign exchange funds to the designated payee in a certain manner in accordance with the remitter's instructions." Article 21(2)(1) stipulates: "Verify whether the payee is a client of this bank or a sub-branch under this bank's jurisdiction based on the account number, address, and other elements. If a remittance for a non-client of this bank is received, it shall be immediately returned to the superior bank; if it is a client of this bank, verify whether the client's detailed name, account number, and other elements are completely consistent with the records retained by this bank; if the payee is a new client locally, verify whether all elements for settlement, including name, address, etc., are accurate and complete." Article 24(2) stipulates: "For funds that cannot be settled, temporary receipts shall be processed on the same day, and inquiries shall be made and records kept in accordance with the relevant provisions of this bank on foreign exchange fund clearing inquiries and replies." Article 29 stipulates: "Upon receiving a message from the remitting bank requesting amendment or stop payment of the remittance instruction, the handling bank shall verify the authenticity of the incoming message and whether the elements such as the relevant business reference number, currency, amount, payee name, etc., are completely consistent with the original remittance instruction." Article 34 stipulates: "Upon receiving an inquiry from the remitting bank or account bank requesting return of remittance, if the funds are in temporary receipt, process the return with backdating; if already settled, seek the payee's opinion and process the return based on the payee's authorization; if the payee refuses the return, state the settlement date of the relevant funds and the fact that the payee refused the return in the reply message." Article 37(2) and (3) stipulate: "(2) Remitting bank requests return of remittance: Upon receiving a notice from the remitting bank requesting return of remittance, the handling bank shall handle it differently based on the following circumstances: If the incoming remittance has not yet been settled, immediately stop the settlement of that remittance, deduct the bank's fees according to the remitting bank's return instructions, and return the funds to the remitting bank. If the incoming remittance has already been settled, our bank must obtain the payee's consent before returning the remittance. If the remittance has been settled and the payee agrees to return it, the payee shall issue a return consent letter, and after confirming that the funds have been credited to our bank's account, deduct relevant fees according to the remitting bank's return instructions and return the funds to the remitting bank. If the remittance has been settled and the payee does not agree to return it, require the payee to issue a written notice of refusal to return the remittance, and our bank will notify the remitting bank based on this, stating the settlement date of the relevant funds and the fact that the payee refused the return in the reply message. (3) Our bank's proactive return of remittance: In the following circumstances, our bank shall proactively return the incoming remittance: 1. Where the payee's name, address, or account number in the incoming remittance instruction is unclear, or for other reasons cannot be settled on time, and after fifteen working days from the issuance of the inquiry, no substantive reply is received and the remittance still cannot be settled; …"

The focal point of dispute at first instance in this case is: Whether the bank, when handling settlement, should bear civil liability for settling in the specific circumstance where the designated payee name was not completely consistent on the surface with the actual payee name.

The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province held at first instance:

The plaintiff, Lucky Pearl Group, is a commercial entity from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and this case is to be handled by reference to the procedures for foreign-related civil litigation. The plaintiff asserts that this case is a dispute over a bank settlement contract, and the defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, does not raise any objection; therefore, the nature of the case can be determined accordingly. Both the plaintiff and the defendant have chosen to apply the law of the People's Republic of China to resolve their substantive dispute. Pursuant to Article 126, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the law of the People's Republic of China shall be the governing law for resolving this dispute.

Telegraphic transfer, as a type of international settlement by remittance, is a method of remittance where the remitting bank, upon application by the remitter, sends a tested cable, telex, or SWIFT message to the overseas receiving bank, instructing it to pay a specified amount to the designated payee. Telegraphic transfer involves four parties, including the remitter, the remitting bank, the receiving bank, and the payee. The dispute in this case arose between the remitter and the receiving bank. The plaintiff, Xibao Group, as the remitter, filled in the payee and receiving bank on the telegraphic transfer application form and entrusted the remitting bank to handle the remittance. The defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, as the receiving bank, had actually released the payment, thereby establishing the cross-border settlement relationship. Although the plaintiff and the defendant did not directly enter into a contract in written or oral form, based on the characteristics of cross-border settlement and the civil acts performed by both parties, it can be determined that the plaintiff and the defendant, as parties to a bank settlement contract relationship, jointly implemented the cross-border settlement with other parties.

The plaintiff, Xibao Group, contended that the defendant, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch, committed serious breaches of contract and regulatory violations during the settlement process. Specifically, it violated Articles 16 and 166 of the Measures for the Settlement of Payments, resulting in a discrepancy between the designated payee and the actual payee; and violated Article 21(2) and Article 37 of the Operational Rules for Foreign Exchange Remittance of the Agricultural Bank of China, failing to fulfill the duties of review, proactive inquiry, and proactive return of remittance, and effecting payment without meeting the conditions for release, thereby causing losses. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province held that Article 2 of the Measures for the Settlement of Payments, issued by the People's Bank of China and effective from December 1, 1997, stipulates: "These Measures apply to the settlement of payments in Renminbi within the territory of the People's Republic of China, unless otherwise provided by the People's Bank of China." This case involves cross-border settlement in US dollars and thus is not subject to these Measures. Article 1 of the Operational Rules for Foreign Exchange Remittance of the Agricultural Bank of China stipulates: "These operational rules are formulated to standardize our bank's foreign exchange remittance operations, prevent and control business risks, and in accordance with relevant international practices and national foreign exchange control regulations." These rules are neither laws, regulations, nor administrative rules; even if violated, they do not automatically constitute a breach of statutory duties. These rules were not incorporated into the cross-border settlement terms of this case and therefore do not automatically become part of the contractual content. The plaintiff argued that these rules represent a commitment to safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the other party to the settlement contract, possessing the significance of a civil commitment. Upon examination, the fundamental reason for the plaintiff's claim that the defendant failed to fulfill its duties of review, proactive inquiry, and proactive return of remittance is that the detailed name of the designated payee, an element requiring review, was not completely consistent with the records retained by the defendant. The defendant, however, argued that although the designated payee's name lacked the word "责任" (liability), "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Company" was the sole entity registered in the Qingdao Administration for Industry and Commerce registration system, its capital account was the sole one existing within the defendant's system, and "Company Limited" and "Limited Liability Company" are merely two expressions of the same legal essence, and the instructions in the SWIFT message could exclude any other payee account. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province held that, given the consistency between the designated payee account number and the actual payee account number, there was a superficial inconsistency between the designated payee, "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Company Limited" (青岛荣星投资管理有限公司), and the actual payee, "Qingdao Rongxing Investment Management Limited Liability Company" (青岛荣星投资管理有限责任公司). However, according to Article 8, paragraph 1 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, which states, "A limited liability company established in accordance with this Law must clearly indicate the words 'limited liability company' or 'company limited' in its company name," this superficial inconsistency does not give rise to ambiguity and should not be deemed a discrepancy. Since there was no situation of an incorrect or unclear payee, the issue of failing to perform proactive inquiry and proactive return of remittance does not arise. As the defendant had already released the payment on March 30, 2009, any subsequent request for return of remittance, whether by the remitter or the remitting bank, requires the consent of the payee before the defendant can process it. The subsequent conversion of foreign exchange after payment release is irrelevant to the nature of the act. It should be noted that although the defendant, as the receiving bank, indeed did not need to review the underlying transaction to determine whether it correctly performed its obligations during the settlement process, when determining rights and responsibilities after a dispute arises, it is necessary to review the underlying transaction for assessment. After all, international settlement is a payment method for settling claims and debts arising from various exchanges between countries (regions) by transferring monetary funds to another country (region) through banks and with the aid of certain credit instruments. As can be seen from the effective judgment, the underlying transaction occurred between the remitter and the actual payee, which sufficiently demonstrates that the superficial inconsistency in the names of the designated payee and the actual payee did not lead to ambiguity, and this is based on facts. Furthermore, when the plaintiff first requested the return of remittance from the defendant through the remitting bank, the reason given by the plaintiff for requesting the return was that the receiving company had no business scope.

Regarding the issue of compensation for losses, Article 113, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations, or performs its contractual obligations in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, causing losses to the other party, the amount of compensation for losses shall be equivalent to the losses caused by the breach, including the benefits obtainable after the performance of the contract, but shall not exceed the losses that the breaching party foresaw or ought to have foreseen as a possible consequence of the breach at the time of entering into the contract." It can be seen that the losses that the plaintiff, Xibao Group, can recover should be losses caused by the defendant's, ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch's, breach of contract. Based on the plaintiff's claims in this case, the claimed amount is the remaining balance after enforcement of the underlying transaction judgment. Although the plaintiff argued that its recourse against the debtor in the underlying transaction was a remedial measure it took, unrelated to the liability of the defendant's conduct, when the same amount has already been satisfied by an effective judgment for payment and then another judgment for payment is sought on other grounds, there is an inherent logical problem regarding which conduct actually caused the losses. The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province held that the direct cause of the losses was the conduct of the debtor in the underlying transaction. Although the cross-border settlement in this case constituted a condition for the underlying transaction, the settlement act itself did not necessarily cause the losses, and there was no objective and necessary causal link between the settlement act and the losses. If the defendant had processed a return of remittance, it might have ultimately avoided the losses. However, based on the plaintiff's statement during court evidence examination, "We deliberately omitted two characters in the telegraphic transfer to induce the defendant to make an inquiry, which would take 10-15 working days, to allow time for the plaintiff's legal representative to visit Qingdao to investigate the true situation of Rongxing Company." Then, the plaintiff could have avoided the so-called losses arising from cross-border settlement at the time of applying for the remittance. By concealing its true intent to circumvent risks in the underlying transaction, the plaintiff caused the defendant to perform the settlement contract in good faith reliance. For the plaintiff to ultimately shift the losses arising from the underlying transaction to the defendant would violate the principle of good faith. The plaintiff's losses were not caused by the defendant's fault, and the defendant is not liable for compensation.

In summary, the plaintiff Xibao Group's claims lack factual and legal basis, and the court does not support them. As for the defendant ABC Qingdao Chengyang Sub-branch's statute of limitations defense, no further review will be conducted. Accordingly, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province, in accordance with Article 60 and Article 125, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 259 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on September 22, 2013:

All claims of the plaintiff Xibao Group Holdings Limited are hereby rejected.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period, and the first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
